plan.angle: Minimum-effort carousel built only from the verified 10-19 Short script, with no new research. Slides: (1) the question; (2) 'No randomized trial has tested semaglutide 7.2 mg against tirzepatide'; (3) SURMOUNT-5 (adults with obesity without diabetes, 72 weeks, maximum tolerated doses), with each drug named next to its number exactly as verified; (4) STEP UP (semaglutide 7.2 mg vs 2.4 mg, adults with obesity without diabetes, 72 weeks, with the estimand named), labelled 'separate trials, not head-to-head'; (5) the dated FDA approval line for 7.2 mg, exactly as verified; (6) common GI side effects and 'don't switch, stop or change your medicines on your own'; (7) disclaimer plus the full prescriber line. No emoji.

package.title: Semaglutide 7.2 mg vs Tirzepatide: Ever Tested Head-to-Head?

social.instagram_caption:
No randomized trial has tested semaglutide 7.2 mg head-to-head against tirzepatide (as of October 2026). Any comparison you see online is indirect.

What we do have is two separate trials:
→ SURMOUNT-5 compared tirzepatide 10 or 15 mg with semaglutide 1.7 or 2.4 mg in adults with obesity, or overweight with a weight-related condition, without diabetes
→ STEP UP tested semaglutide 7.2 mg against 2.4 mg and placebo in adults with obesity without diabetes

Different trials, different people, different comparisons, so their numbers can't be lined up directly. Only a randomized trial testing both drugs together can answer which works better.

In SURMOUNT-5, gastrointestinal effects such as nausea, diarrhoea, constipation and vomiting were the most common with both drugs, mostly mild to moderate.

Save this for the next time a headline claims one "beats" the other.

#GLP1 #Semaglutide #Tirzepatide #SURMOUNT5 #STEPUP #MetabolicHealth #ObesityResearch

Not personal advice. Don't switch, stop or change your medicines on your own. Talk to your doctor or prescriber about whether it's right for you.

factcheck.summary:
I checked every number against the source abstracts (Europe PMC records for PMIDs 40353578 and 40961952) and they all match. The carousel passes with three small wording fixes.

**SURMOUNT-5 (NEJM 2025)**
- Group sizes 374 vs 377 (751 in total), open-label, 72 weeks.
- Tirzepatide at the highest tolerated dose (10 or 15 mg) vs semaglutide at the highest tolerated dose (1.7 or 2.4 mg).
- Average weight change -20.2% vs -13.7%; waist change -18.4 cm vs -13.0 cm.
- Stomach and gut (gastrointestinal) side effects were the most common in both groups, mostly mild to moderate.

**STEP UP (Lancet Diabetes & Endocrinology 2025)**
- 1,407 adults with obesity, 72 weeks, counting everyone randomized (treatment-policy estimand).
- Average weight loss 18.7% on 7.2 mg vs 15.6% on 2.4 mg vs 3.9% on placebo.
- Gastrointestinal side effects 70.8% vs 61.2% vs 42.8%.

**Other checks**
- The core claim holds: no randomized trial has compared semaglutide 7.2 mg with tirzepatide. Coverage of the EASD meeting says only an indirect comparison (SURMOUNT-1 vs STEP UP) exists.
- "Approval of 7.2 mg varies by country" is accurate. FDA approval of higher-dose Wegovy was reported in March 2026.
- Framing is good throughout: indirect vs head-to-head is clear, populations and estimands are stated, side effects are shown, and the slides carry "don't switch, stop or change your medicines on your own", "Not personal advice" and the prescriber line.
- The title's question is answered on slide 2.

The remaining issues are minor label precision only.

issues.claim: Columns: 'Semaglutide 2.4 mg (max)'; headline 'SURMOUNT-5: tirzepatide vs semaglutide 2.4 mg'
issues.problem: In SURMOUNT-5 the semaglutide group took the highest dose each person could tolerate, either 1.7 or 2.4 mg, and the items row on this same slide already says so. Labelling the whole group '2.4 mg (max)' slightly overstates the dose and doesn't match the slide's own rows.
issues.fix: Headline: 'SURMOUNT-5: tirzepatide vs semaglutide (up to 2.4 mg)'. Columns: ["Tirzepatide 10 or 15 mg", "Semaglutide 1.7 or 2.4 mg"]

issues.claim: Common side effects in SURMOUNT-5 (tirzepatide vs semaglutide 2.4 mg)
issues.problem: Same dose-label problem: the semaglutide group took 1.7 or 2.4 mg.
issues.fix: Common side effects in SURMOUNT-5 (tirzepatide vs semaglutide 1.7 or 2.4 mg)

issues.problem: The headline says 'average weight loss', but the individual bars don't say what they measure. A viewer who sees one bar on its own (the muted-viewer test) could read it as a typical result rather than an average across the group.
issues.fix: Set each item's detail to 'Average weight loss, 72 weeks, STEP UP'.
